districtFact: Kent School District's one-page Student Calendar uses separate dates for the K–12, kindergarten, preschool, and ECSE schedules. It also combines a recurring two-hour Wednesday early release with three-hour conference dismissals for specific grade levels and an ordered sequence of optional snow make-up days.

about.title: About Kent School District
about.content: Kent School District serves students in South King County, Washington. Its Student Calendar is designed around a 180-day year and separates the general school opening from kindergarten and preschool starts, while also identifying ECSE program dates that do not apply to every student.

about.title: Wednesday and Conference Release Schedules
about.content: KSD marks a two-hour early release for all schools on Wednesdays during the student year. Conference weeks add three-hour early dismissals for elementary students, a separate secondary conference day adds a three-hour secondary dismissal, and the final day uses a three-hour early release for all schools. Exact clock times still come from each school's bell schedule.

about.title: Snow Make-Up Order Matters
about.content: The calendar does not treat every reserved snow date as an automatic attendance day. It names an April date first, a May date second, and then allows additional make-up time after the scheduled end of school in June if closures require it. Families should wait for a KSD announcement before changing plans.

planningTips.title: Kent School District Calendar Notes
content: The general first day, kindergarten first day, and preschool first day are different. Use the date for the student's program.
Wednesdays use a recurring two-hour early-release schedule for all schools. Confirm exact bell and bus times with the student's school.
Elementary and secondary conference dismissals are not interchangeable. Conference weeks affect elementary schools, while one November conference date applies to secondary schools.
ECSE can have extra no-school conference dates and an earlier last day. Do not assume the K–12 last day applies to ECSE programs.
Optional snow days remain non-school days unless KSD activates them after a cancellation. The district uses the April date first, then the May date, and may extend the year in June.
The district calendar page points families to school websites and the KSD mobile app for school-specific events that do not appear in the one-page student calendar.

districtFaqs.q: Does Kent School District release students early on Wednesdays?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. KSD's Student Calendar marks a recurring two-hour early release for all schools on Wednesdays during the school year. Check the school's bell schedule for the exact dismissal and transportation time.

districtFaqs.q: Do Kent kindergarten and preschool students start on the first K–12 day?
districtFaqs.a: No. KSD publishes separate first days for the general student calendar, kindergarten, and preschool. The dates change by school year, so use the opening schedule on the current calendar.

districtFaqs.q: How do KSD conference early dismissals work?
districtFaqs.a: Elementary conference weeks use three-hour early dismissals for elementary schools only. A separate November secondary conference date uses a three-hour early dismissal for secondary schools only.

districtFaqs.q: Does ECSE follow every date on the KSD calendar?
districtFaqs.a: No. The calendar can list extra ECSE no-school conference dates and an ECSE last day that comes before the K–12 last day. Families should follow the ECSE-specific labels.

districtFaqs.q: Are Kent's optional snow days automatic school days?
districtFaqs.a: No. They are reserved make-up dates. KSD lists an April date, then a May date, and may add days after the scheduled June ending if needed. Check district closure updates before treating one as an attendance day.

districtFaqs.q: Where should families check for school-specific Kent events?
districtFaqs.a: Use the individual school's website or the Kent School District mobile app. The one-page Student Calendar focuses on districtwide dates and selected program exceptions.
